title: Your first incident
briefing: "The daily report didn't arrive this morning.
It worked yesterday. Please fix ASAP!!"
Nobody knows what changed. Time to investigate.
expert_briefing: Ticket #4711 (Finance, priority: high): "daily report missing, fix ASAP".
tips: Observe, form a hypothesis, change ONE thing, verify. Start by running the program and reading what it says.
Failing programs usually write down why, in a log under /var/log.
hints: Run the script and read its output. Then find its log in /var/log — failing programs leave notes.
`grep ERROR /var/log/reportd.log` shows two separate problems: a directory that doesn't exist, and a config file nobody can read. `ls -l /opt/reportd` tells you who owns what.
`mkdir ~/reports`, then `chmod u+r /opt/reportd/report.conf` (you own it), then run `/opt/reportd/run_report.sh` again.
solution:
/opt/reportd/run_report.sh
grep ERROR /var/log/reportd.log
mkdir ~/reports
ls -l /opt/reportd
chmod u+r /opt/reportd/report.conf
/opt/reportd/run_report.sh

lines: # reportd: builds the daily sales report for Finance.

reactions.say: Permission denied — on a file this time, not the script. Who owns report.conf? What are its permissions?
One problem down. Run the script again — does it get further this time?
Logs are gold. Notice the ERROR lines — there may be more than one kind.

explanation: That was a real incident workflow: reproduce the failure, read the logs, form a hypothesis, fix one thing, verify, repeat. Two independent root causes — a missing output directory and an unreadable config — fixed with the tools you learned today. You own report.conf, so you could restore its read bit without being root. That's the job.
